sources.title: Gemini API Additional Terms of Service | Google AI for Developers
sources.claim: Current Gemini API Additional Terms: age, professional/business purpose, API Client definition and EEA Paid Services restriction; distinct Unpaid/Paid definitions and data-use/retention clauses; financial-advice disclaimer.
evidence: Effective March 23, 2026
Last updated 2026-04-28 UTC.
Use of Google AI Studio and Gemini API is for developers building with Google AI models for professional or business purposes, not for consumer use.

You must be 18 years of age or older to use the APIs. You also will not use the Services as part of a website, application, or other service (collectively, "**API Clients**") that is directed towards or is likely to be accessed by individuals under the age of 18.
You may use only Paid Services when making API Clients available to users in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, or the United Kingdom.
Any Services that are offered free of charge like direct interactions with Google AI Studio or unpaid quota in Gemini API are unpaid Services (the "**Unpaid Services**").

If you're in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, or the United Kingdom, the terms under "How Google uses Your Data" in "Paid Services" apply to all Services, including Google AI Studio and unpaid quota in the Gemini API, even though they are offered free of charge.
Your access to Gemini API is a "Paid Service" only when accessing the API through a Cloud Project associated with an active billing account.

For Paid Services, Google logs prompts and responses for a limited period of time, solely for detecting and preventing violations of the Prohibited Use Policy to maintain the safety and security of the Services, and any required legal or regulatory disclosures.

When using Grounding with Google Search, Google will store prompts, contextual information that you may provide, and output for thirty (30) days for the purposes of creating Grounded Results and Search Suggestions and the stored information can be used for debugging and testing of systems that support Grounding with Google Search.

When you use Paid Services, including, for example, the paid quota of the Gemini API, Google doesn't use your prompts (including associated system instructions, cached content, and files such as images, videos, or documents) or responses to improve our products

Don't rely on the Services for medical, mental health, legal, financial, or other professional advice. Any content regarding those topics is provided for informational purposes only, does not constitute medical diagnosis or treatment, and is not a substitute for advice from a qualified professional.
sources.verification: Direct official page retrieved in full through web_extract. Browser checked the English page at the final URL and the automatic Spanish locale variant; the EEA Paid Services clause appears under Use Restrictions, adjacent to the professional/business and available-region text. No terms were accepted and no API call was made.

sources.title: Google APIs Terms of Service | Google for Developers
sources.claim: Underlying API Terms incorporated by the Gemini Additional Terms; privacy policy, submitted-content license, confidentiality of API credentials, and additional terms control in case of conflict.
evidence: Last modified: November 9, 2021
If there is a conflict between these terms and additional terms applicable to a given API, the additional terms will control for that conflict.

For the sole purpose of enabling Google to provide, secure, and improve the APIs (and the related service(s)) and only in accordance with the applicable Google privacy policies, you give Google a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, sublicensable, royalty-free, and non-exclusive license to Use content submitted, posted, or displayed to or from the APIs through your API Client.

Developer credentials (such as passwords, keys, and client IDs) are intended to be used by you and identify your API Client. You will keep your credentials confidential and make reasonable efforts to prevent and discourage other API Clients from using your credentials. Developer credentials may not be embedded in open source projects.

You will provide and adhere to a privacy policy for your API Client that clearly and accurately describes to users of your API Client what user information you collect and how you use and share such information (including for advertising) with Google and third parties.
sources.verification: Full official Google APIs Terms page retrieved and saved. Current page states last modified November 9, 2021; the Gemini Additional Terms page incorporates it and provides the conflict rule. No API use or acceptance performed.

evidence: A cost-efficient model, optimized for high-volume agentic tasks, translation, and simple data processing.

sources.title: Rate limits | Gemini API - Google AI for Developers
sources.claim: Limits are RPM, input TPM and RPD, applied per project; active rates are displayed in AI Studio, can change, and are not capacity guarantees.
evidence: Rate limits are usually measured across three dimensions: Requests per minute (RPM), Tokens per minute (input) (TPM), Requests per day (RPD).
Rate limits are applied per project, not per API key. Requests per day (RPD) quotas reset at midnight Pacific time.

Rate limits depend on a variety of factors (such as your usage tier) and can be viewed in Google AI Studio. As your tier and account status change over time, your rate limits will automatically update. Specified rate limits are not guaranteed and actual capacity may vary.
sources.verification: Official rate-limit documentation retrieved in full. The documentation routes current project-specific interactive rates to the AI Studio panel and says actual capacity may vary; panel not opened and account-specific limits remain unverified.

sources.title: Billing | Gemini API | Google AI for Developers
sources.claim: New accounts start in Free Tier and receive a project/API key by default; Free is available in EEA regions. Paid Tier setup requires Cloud Billing, payment method and, for prepay, at least $5 or equivalent.
evidence: New accounts begin on the Free Tier, which allows access to certain models in the Gemini API and AI Studio, up to the models' free tier rate limits.
New users will have a project and API key created for them by default.
Upgrading from the Free Tier to the Paid Tier means linking a billing account and prepaying to add a minimum of $5 (or equivalent in other currencies) of credits to your account.

If you've never set up a Google billing account before: You'll be asked to select your country to agree to the Terms of Service. Then, fill in or confirm your contact information and payment method to continue.

Can I use the Gemini API for free in EEA (including EU), the UK, and CH?

Yes, we make the free tier and paid tier available in many regions.
sources.verification: Official billing documentation and EEA FAQ retrieved; English page and key instructions saved. The page documents project/key defaults and the Paid Tier payment path but contains no explicit no-credit-card guarantee for an individual Free Tier signup. No account was created and no onboarding panel was tested.

sources.title: Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy
sources.claim: Finance use is restricted when AI makes unsupervised automated decisions with material detrimental impact on individual rights; deceptive claims of financial expertise are prohibited; educational exceptions are discretionary and policy-specific.
evidence: Makes automated decisions that have a material detrimental impact on individual rights without human supervision in high-risk domains -- for example, in employment, healthcare, finance, legal, housing, insurance, or social welfare.
3. Facilitating misleading claims of expertise or capability in sensitive areas -- for example in health, finance, government services, or the law, in order to deceive.
We may make exceptions to these policies based on educational, documentary, scientific, or artistic considerations, or where harms are outweighed by substantial benefits to the public.
sources.verification: Full official policy page retrieved. The academic/educational exception is discretionary policy text, not an exception to the separate EEA Paid Services requirement or the professional/business restriction in Gemini Additional Terms.
